findings.title: Dynamic imports are eagerly executed for every app
findings.body: All `import(...)` expressions are evaluated immediately when the `appStore` object literal is constructed, so importing `appStore` starts loading all 29 app modules regardless of which app is actually needed. This defeats the stated lazy/async-import purpose, retains the startup/bundle-loading cost for every consumer, and creates promises for unused apps whose rejection (e.g. a broken optional app) would be an unhandled rejection since nothing ever awaits that entry. Imports should only be initiated on access, e.g. via factory functions `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` with callers awaiting the factory.

findings.title: Calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget and outside the try/catch
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` discards the promises returned by the async callback. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) therefore cannot catch errors from `await getCalendar(...)` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, and `Reschedule` can return and send the reschedule email before the old calendar/video events are deleted, leaving orphaned events; on serverless runtimes the deletions may never run at all. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

findings.title: Calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget and outside the try/catch
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` discards the promises returned by the async callback. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) therefore cannot catch errors from `await getCalendar(...)` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, and `Reschedule` can return and send the reschedule email before the old calendar/video events are deleted, leaving orphaned events; on serverless runtimes the deletions may never run at all. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletions are not awaited before mutation completes
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` discards all returned promises. The mutation proceeds immediately to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns while deletions are still pending (and any failure becomes an unhandled rejection), so the old calendar/video event can survive a successful reschedule response. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race with apiDeletes consumption
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, deletions are pushed into `apiDeletes` from inside a `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` callback. Because `getCalendar` is now async, none of these pushes happen synchronously, so the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 (and the `await apiDeletes` at line 617) typically snapshot an empty/incomplete array. The handler can finish and the process can terminate before the external calendar events are deleted. Await the per-credential work with `Promise.all`/`for...of` and push the deletion promises before they are consumed.
